Photograph: Stefan Rousseau/PA Metropolitan police Met police incapable of change, says mother of murdered sisters after Simon Levy case Mina Smallman, whose daughters were killed in north London park in 2020, says force ‘decides who matters’ Helena Horton Thu 13 Aug 2026 04.31 EDT First published on Thu 13 Aug 2026 03.41 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The Metropolitan police does not take all cases of violence against women seriously and instead “decides who matters”, the mother of two murdered women has said. Mina Smallman, whose daughters Bibaa Henry and Nicole Smallman were killed in a north London park in 2020, also said Britain’s biggest police force was incapable of change. Two police officers were jailed in 2021 after taking photographs of the dead bodies of her daughters and sharing the images in WhatsApp groups, referring to them as “dead birds”. Commenting on the case of the sex offender Simon Levy, 40, who was left free to kill two women after police failings, she said: “One of the women that were murdered, because she was a sex worker, she wasn’t taken seriously. They didn’t look into her murder until he murdered a mother of four, and then they joined the two cases together. “How ridiculous is that. Once again, the Met is deciding who matters. Both those women’s lives were important to their families, how dare they decide that they weren’t going to look into that case.” Levy, who this week was given a whole-life sentence for his crimes, was also convicted earlier this year of sexually assaulting 11 other women, 10 of them on trains and the underground in London between 2023 and 2025. Smallman said she had been in contact with the head of the Metropolitan police, Sir Mark Rowley, after reading about the case. She told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme: “After reading this case I sent a text message to Sir Mark and said: ‘How many times are you going to stand up publicly and apologise for failures in the Met?’ “It becomes a joke. The truth is, the Metropolitan police is too big for any senior team to be able to have a hands-on understanding of the day-to-day activities of that organisation.” She said the Met was incapable of change because it was “too big”. “I believe that Sir Mark Rowley wants to change the Met and wants to do things differently, but they haven’t got a clue.” She added: “We are asking them to do too much, they haven’t got the finances, it has become riddled with inactivity, corruption, misogyny, racism, and they just can’t do it.” The crime and policing minister Sarah Jones previously described Levy as a monster and said the failings that had allowed him to remain free were “deeply concerning”. Jones signalled the government would allow the relevant institutions and police watchdog to establish what had gone wrong. “The fact that Levy was able to inflict such devastating harm after being freed by police and the courts is deeply concerning,” she said. “It raises serious questions that require urgent answers.” Rowley denied that the Met had not done enough, saying: “The inference that the Met didn’t try on this death is not true, the Met tried.” But he said he did not understand why the Prison Service released Simon Levy after he sexually assaulted one of its staff members in jail. Levy was questioned by police about the assault five months after his release, which Rowley said was “too slow”. He told the Today programme: “That’s one of the things we’ve apologised for, but of course there are two mistakes in that: you’ve got he was released on licence by the Prison Service, having sexually assaulted in prison one of its people, I don’t understand that decision either. “I’m prepared to come here and be accountable, we’ve got two officers being referred to be investigated by the independent office of police complaints, we take our accountability seriously. “The rest of the system is not doing that. The Prison Service should not have released somebody who’s indecently assaulting its staff.” Explore more on these topics Metropolitan police Violence against women and girls Police London Sex work Crime England news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Complaints filed to police watchdog over Met’s handling of Al Fayed abuse allegations Met gets extension to AI project after Sadiq Khan blocked deal Met police chief calls for law to make stolen phones ‘unusable bricks’ Met warns about hate speech at Unite the Kingdom and Palestine marches Met officers investigated over handling of Mohamed Al Fayed abuse complaints Met sets up specialist unit as antisemitic hate crimes in London hit two-year high Met investigates hundreds of officers after using Palantir AI tool Met says it will resume arresting people who show support for Palestine Action Met accused of insulting black people with shake-up of anti-racism strategy Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

https://www.thewrap.com/creative-content.text: Getting your Trinity Audio player ready… There are few actresses as fearless as Léa Seydoux. She anchored controversial 2017 Cannes-winner “Blue Is the Warmest Color,” appeared in David Cronenberg’s abrasive “Crimes of the Future” and popped in for a pair of Wes Anderson wonders (“The Grand Budapest Hotel” and “The French Dispatch”), while also co-starring in giant Hollywood blockbusters – a “Dune” movie (“Dune: Part Two”), two 007 movies (“Spectre” and “No Time to Die”) and “Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol.” At this year’s Toronto Film Festival she stars in “Gentle Monster,” a hot-button drama that premiered at this year’s Cannes Film Festival and will be on Netflix later this year. In the film, Seydoux plays an experimental musician married to filmmaker (Laurence Rupp), who, following a psychological episode, relocates from Munich to the countryside. “But their bucolic idyll collapses when a sex crimes unit, led by officer Else Kühn (Jella Haase), arrives to seize the family’s digital devices — and to arrest Philip. As the case against him becomes increasingly difficult to deny, her attention shifts to her son Johnny — and the terrifying possibility that he might be involved,” reads the official TIFF program. Read Next 'Gentle Monster' Review: Léa Seydoux Ponders Moral Duties in Chilling, Emotional Drama Seydoux told Jada Yuan at TheWrap’s studio at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival that she was actually worried she might not get the role – not because she was anxious about the subject matter but because she had trouble scheduling a meeting with her writer-director Marie Kreutzer. “I was like, she will never hire me for this movie because I’m always postponing the call . You were very relaxed on the Zoom, and I was surprised because sometimes directors can be nervous because your movie is a baby that you cherish,” she said. There are some nude scenes in “Gentle Monster” and Seydoux said they spoke about what that would look like, as Seydoux told the director she’d just had a baby and was in “a certain shape.” “I thought it was good to show a real body. You remember we spoke about this. It’s also something that I like in the film I have to say now – this intimacy of this couple that is shown, and it makes it even more tragic because they are really relatable,” Seydoux said. The normalcy of their relationship, Seydoux said, helps to demystify what a pedophile is. “Sometimes you imagine the guy behind the bush. It’s not that. It can happen to anyone. And the way Marie wrote the script, I thought was very subtle, also because of that, because we understand the complexity of this woman who’s facing this situation, and she’s pulled apart between different feelings,” said Seydoux. “She’s always fighting against contradictory emotions, and that I thought was extremely interesting.” Read Next ‘Carrie’ Creator Mike Flanagan Also Wasn’t Sure About the Streaming Series

https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/reun.text: Guvernul francez găzduieşte luni, la Paris, o „conferinţă a donatorilor” pentru a strânge fondurile rămase necesare pentru repararea structurii de protecţie de la centrala nucleară dezafectată de la Cernobîl, avariată în urma unui atac cu dronă rusească la începutul anului 2025. „Am strâns puţin peste jumătate din suma necesară. Această conferinţă este a doua etapă către obţinerea sumei de 500 de milioane de euro necesare, cu obiectivul de a finaliza proiectul până în primăvara anului 2027”, a declarat pentru AFP biroul ministrului francez al economiei, Roland Lescure, potrivit Agerpres. Ministrul a afirmat la mijlocul lunii octombrie că „ţările G7 au strâns deja sau sunt în curs de a strânge 260 de milioane de euro”. Guvernul francez subliniază în invitaţia sa la conferinţă că „amploarea şi complexitatea” pagubelor cauzate de atacul rusesc „fac ca restaurarea completă să fie atât urgentă, cât şi dificilă”. Evenimentul, co-organizat de guvernul ucrainean şi Banca Europeană pentru Reconstrucţie şi Dezvoltare (BERD), „va reprezenta ocazia de a prezenta cele mai recente evaluări tehnice şi strategia de restaurare propusă, precum şi de a face bilanţul angajamentelor internaţionale existente, în vederea asigurării unor noi promisiuni de contribuţii substanţiale la programul de restaurare”, se adaugă în comunicat. „Sperăm să primim luni noi contribuţii, pe care ţările le-ar putea anunţa în cursul zilei”, a precizat biroul ministrului economiei. Anatolii Kutsevol, adjunctul ministrului ucrainean al energiei, va fi de asemenea prezent la conferinţa de la Paris, iar premierul Serhii Koreţki va participa prin videoconferinţă. Evenimentul va fi închis de Benjamin Haddad, ministrul delegat al Franţei pentru Europa. Reactorul nuclear de la Cernobîl, care a explodat în aprilie 1986, a fost izolat în 2016 cu o structură metalică de protecţie, care acoperă primul sarcofag de beton construit în grabă în 1986. În februarie 2025, această structură a fost avariată de o dronă rusească. Franţa, care deţine în acest an preşedinţia G7, a indicat în martie că suma necesară pentru reparaţii se ridică la „circa 500 de milioane de euro”. Statele Unite au anunţat la sfârşitul lunii aprilie că vor debloca „până la 100 de milioane de dolari” şi au cerut partenerilor săi din G7 să le urmeze exemplul.
